points.requirement: **A checkpoint inhibitor removes one brake from T cells that already recognize the cancer. In early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), adding pembrolizumab to chemotherapy raised the complete-response rate and improved survival, whether or not the tumor stained for PD-L1.**

points.entailment: Specific inhibitory contacts and overlapping CTLA-4/PD-1 emphases are distinguished from guaranteed restoration of every pre-existing tumour-reactive cell. The early-TNBC regimen comparison does not select individual benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Checkpoint antibodies interrupt specified inhibitory contacts. PD-1 is a receptor with two partners, PD-L1 and PD-L2; PD-L1 is a distinct molecule found on cancer and non-cancer cells. The pembrolizumab label describes blockade of PD-1 binding to both ligands. Atezolizumab instead binds PD-L1 and blocks its PD-1 and B7.1 interactions; directly blocking PD-L1 does not directly block the separate PD-1/PD-L2 contact. These target-specific descriptions are more precise than treating all checkpoint drugs as one switch.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: CTLA-4 is often emphasised during priming in lymphoid sites and PD-1 during ongoing responses in tissues. These are overlapping emphases, not exclusive addresses: CD28-related regulation can also matter later. LAG-3, TIM-3 and TIGIT have their own biology rather than being interchangeable versions of PD-1. A regulator identified in an experimental model does not establish benefit from blocking it in another population; each intervention needs its own evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: KEYNOTE-522 randomised 1,174 people with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to pembrolizumab or placebo with chemotherapy before surgery, followed by continuation of the assigned antibody or placebo after surgery. At a median follow-up of 75.1 months, estimated 60-month overall survival was 86.6 per cent versus 81.7 per cent. Enrolment did not require PD-L1 positivity. The trial compared the whole perioperative regimen and was not designed to isolate the contribution of each treatment phase. These group results do not predict one person's outcome.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Exhaustion is a distinct differentiation programme associated with persistent stimulation, altered function, multiple inhibitory receptors and transcriptional and chromatin changes. Mouse TOX experiments identified a central regulator of this programme. It is neither brief tiredness, every weak assay, anergy nor a DNA sequence change. Deficits can be graded and subsets retain different capacities.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In chronic LCMV infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor exhausted cells self-renewed and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-L1 blockade. points.heading: The brake that the tumor borrows
points.requirement: Tumors often display PD-L1 *because* T cells are attacking them. T cells that recognize a tumor release interferon gamma, and interferon gamma induces PD-L1 on nearby tumor and immune cells. This is called **[adaptive immune resistance](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/tumor-immunology/adaptive-immune-resistance)**: the brake is pulled in response to the attack ([Taube et al., 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22461641/)). That is why PD-L1 staining and a [lymphocyte-rich "hot" pattern](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/tumor-immunology/hot-excluded-cold-tumor) often travel together.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.

PD-L1 is not the only brake that follows the attack. Spranger and colleagues found in human melanoma that the T-cell-inflamed tumours were the ones with high indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), PD-L1 and regulatory T cells, and in mice that all three depended on CD8 T cells being present: IDO and PD-L1 through interferon gamma, and regulatory T cells through CCR4-binding chemokines with some induced proliferation. Their reading was that these pathways are driven by the immune response rather than orchestrated by the cancer cells.

Evidence from tissue. In human melanocytic lesions, 98% of PD-L1-positive (B7-H1-positive) tumours had tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes compared with 28% of PD-L1-negative tumours; positive melanocytes sat almost always immediately next to lymphocytes, and interferon gamma was detected at the interface but not in PD-L1-negative tumours (Taube and colleagues). The same colocalisation appeared in inflamed benign naevi, which fits PD-L1 as a response to tissue inflammation. In triple-negative breast cancer, Gruosso and colleagues described an immunoreactive group whose tumours had granzyme B-positive CD8 T cells inside cancer-cell regions, a type 1 interferon signature and elevated IDO and PD-L1, the pattern adaptive resistance predicts; that is an association in tissue and not a direct test of the loop. The alternative, called innate or constitutive resistance, is PD-L1 driven by the cancer cell's own signalling regardless of T cells.

A functionally important loss of JAK1 or JAK2 can impair the tumour cell response to interferon gamma. In four people with metastatic melanoma that relapsed on anti-PD-1 treatment, two relapse samples carried loss-of-function JAK1 or JAK2 mutations with deletion of the remaining normal allele, and truncating JAK1 or JAK2 mutations left the cells unresponsive to interferon gamma (Zaretsky and colleagues). The JAK2-deficient relapse cells lost interferon-gamma-induced PD-L1 and class-I increases but retained responses to interferon alfa and beta. In engineered melanoma cells, JAK1 or JAK2 loss did not abolish recognition by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Loss of inducibility is therefore different from absence of all baseline recognition. This selected series does not estimate a frequency for all cancers.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A PD-L1 stain measures protein on defined tumour and immune cells, not why it is present. Colocalization with lymphocytes and interferon-related expression can support induced expression, while a uniform lymphocyte-poor pattern raises other hypotheses; neither pattern proves a cause. Adding interferon gamma and measuring PD-L1 tests inducibility in a laboratory model. Appropriate pathway perturbations and controls investigate causation, and neither that assay nor a tissue score measures the entire in-vivo feedback loop or treatment benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

These are observations about identity and location. Some infiltrating T cells recognize viral or other non-cancer antigens; others restrain responses. Region, specimen, disease site and sampling time matter, and treatment can change the pattern. Neither a small biopsy nor a pattern label describes every site in a person or selects an immunotherapy. Exclusion suggests questions about recruitment, vessels, matrix and local cells, rather than proving one causal wall.

points.entailment: Missing genetic machinery is not rebuilt and a new receptor is not installed. Regulated expression, responding populations and local chemokine dependence can change, so the source table is qualified rather than assigning PD-1 only one late physical step.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Checkpoint blockade changes an inhibitory interaction; it does not install a new recognition receptor or reconstruct required HLA machinery that has been genetically lost. That last statement concerns missing machinery, not a claim that checkpoint treatment can never affect regulated HLA expression. Recognition, access and cell state remain separate dependencies. Vaccines, engineered cell receptors and cytokines change different inputs, and a plausible combination still needs regimen-specific benefit and safety evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Naive, effector, memory and exhausted populations describe response histories and differentiation programmes, not one mandatory sequence for every T cell. Anergy and exhaustion are distinct mechanisms. Regulatory function is a separate role. Identity, location, receptor specificity, state and measured function are complementary observations.

In chronic viral infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor populations sustained responses and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-1 blockade. In tumour models, progenitor exhausted cells differed from terminally exhausted cells; the related melanoma observations were associations rather than a universal treatment-selection rule. Progenitor-like exhaustion is not ordinary memory. A shared receptor does not require a shared functional phenotype, and PD-1 or TCF1 alone does not establish state or tumour specificity.

Paired human skin-cancer biopsies after PD-1 blockade showed expanded clonotypes not previously observed in the same tumour, supporting clonal replacement as another response model. Absence from an earlier sample does not establish absence throughout the body. A fictional PD-1-positive population near cancer can include viral-reactive and tumour-peptide-reactive cells. Neither proximity nor peptide response proves natural tumour recognition or killing. Preserve response history, sampling site, time, multiple markers and controlled function; neither division nor a favourable pattern predicts individual benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: At the fourth planned interim analysis reported in 2022, median follow-up was 39.1 months and all 1,174 participants contributed to the assigned-group survival comparison. coverageEvidence.excerpt: KEYNOTE-522 randomised 1,174 people with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to pembrolizumab or placebo with chemotherapy before surgery, followed by continuation of the assigned antibody or placebo after surgery. coverageEvidence.excerpt: The combined positive score is the number of PD-L1-staining tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages divided by the total number of viable tumour cells, multiplied by 100 (Cortes 2022). KEYNOTE-355 randomised 847 patients with untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer 2:1 to pembrolizumab or placebo with the investigator's chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine-carboplatin), with PD-L1 tested centrally by the 22C3 assay. Progression-free survival at the interim analysis was 9.7 against 5.6 months in the CPS 10 or more group (hazard ratio 0.65, primary objective met), 7.6 against 5.6 months in CPS 1 or more (0.74, not significant) and 7.5 against 5.6 months overall (0.82, not tested), the effect increasing with PD-L1 enrichment (Cortes 2020). At the final analysis (median follow-up 44.1 months) overall survival in the CPS 10 group was 23.0 against 16.1 months (hazard ratio 0.73, significant), 17.6 against 16.0 months in CPS 1 or more (0.86, not significant) and 17.2 against 15.5 months in all patients (0.89, not tested); grade 3 to 5 treatment-related events occurred in 68.1 against 66.9 percent (Cortes 2022). NICE recommends pembrolizumab with paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel for untreated triple-negative locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic breast cancer in the population the appraisal covers (TA801, June 2022). A different assay and score defined the earlier atezolizumab result: IMpassion130 used the SP142 immune-cell score with positivity at 1 percent or more of the tumour area; median progression-free survival was 7.5 against 5.0 months and overall survival 25.0 against 15.5 months in the PD-L1-positive subgroup, without a significant overall survival gain in the whole population (Schmid 2018), and the parent page's history records that approval was later withdrawn. Early disease needs no PD-L1 test: in KEYNOTE-522 pembrolizumab with chemotherapy raised pathological complete response from 51.2 to 64.8 percent in stage II and III disease unselected for PD-L1 (Schmid 2020) and five-year overall survival from 81.7 to 86.6 percent (Schmid 2024); NICE TA851 (December 2022) recommends it for triple-negative early or locally advanced breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. The biomarker readout pd-l1-cps carries the label wording for every CPS threshold across cancers.

points.heading: The cost: immune-related adverse events
points.requirement: Releasing a brake that protects healthy tissue can cause inflammation in any organ. These [immune-related adverse events (irAEs)](/wiki/education/concepts/therapeutics/toxicities-and-supportive-care/immune-related-adverse-event) usually appear during treatment but can start after it ends. Across 2,799 patients given pembrolizumab alone in trials, hypothyroidism occurred in 8% and adrenal insufficiency in 0.8%. In KEYNOTE-522, pembrolizumab was stopped for adverse reactions in 20% of patients, and the label asks for blood cortisol checks before surgery in this setting ([FDA label, sections 5.1 and 6.1](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/125514s194lbl.pdf)).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The October 2026 U.S. label separates safety populations. Among 2,799 single-agent recipients in pooled melanoma and lung-cancer trials, hypothyroidism occurred in 8% (237/2,799) and adrenal insufficiency in 0.8% (22/2,799). Those are not TNBC-specific rates. In KEYNOTE-522, 778 people received pembrolizumab with the perioperative strategy, and adverse reactions led to its discontinuation in 20%. Immune-mediated reactions can begin after stopping treatment. For neoadjuvant TNBC use, the label calls for blood cortisol monitoring at baseline, before surgery and when clinically indicated; these labelled monitoring instructions are separate from a prediction of individual benefit or harm.
coverageEvidence.sourceScope: Selected complete raw SPL v229 paragraphs/tables: indications, mechanism, immune-mediated harms, safety-pool definitions and KEYNOTE-522/355 results. No whole-label reading. July supplement 194 is an older label and does not replace October v229.

The prescribing information warns that immune-mediated reactions can arise after treatment stops and that hypothyroidism may require long-term hormone replacement. coverageEvidence.excerpt: The multiple-controls analogy has two possible branches: interrupting regulation can support useful cancer-directed activity and can also injure healthy tissue. Neither outcome is guaranteed for a person. Normal checkpoint regulation helps limit immune injury, and immune-related adverse events can involve several organs. Assess activity, durability and harms in the relevant population rather than equating more immune activity with exclusively tumour-directed benefit.

points.requirement: - **Reading "hot" as "will respond".** A lymphocyte-rich tumor is prognostically favorable, but escape by HLA or B2M loss can still block the drug's route.

points.entailment: A lymphocyte-rich pattern is not a guaranteed response, and lost required display remains a separate dependency; prognosis is bounded to its cohort and assay.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

These are observations about identity and location. Some infiltrating T cells recognize viral or other non-cancer antigens; others restrain responses. Region, specimen, disease site and sampling time matter, and treatment can change the pattern. Neither a small biopsy nor a pattern label describes every site in a person or selects an immunotherapy. Exclusion suggests questions about recruitment, vessels, matrix and local cells, rather than proving one causal wall.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are lymphocytes found in sampled tumour tissue, including T- and B-cell populations. The breast stromal TIL method estimates the area occupied by a defined mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate within eligible tumour-associated stroma on H&E sections. Higher pretreatment scores were associated with better outcomes in the cited early triple-negative breast cancer cohorts, but those associations do not guarantee an individual outcome or establish extra benefit from pembrolizumab. Intratumoral location, stromal area, immune-cell counts and cells expanded for TIL therapy are different measurements or uses.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Checkpoint blockade changes an inhibitory interaction; it does not install a new recognition receptor or reconstruct required HLA machinery that has been genetically lost. That last statement concerns missing machinery, not a claim that checkpoint treatment can never affect regulated HLA expression. Recognition, access and cell state remain separate dependencies. Vaccines, engineered cell receptors and cytokines change different inputs, and a plausible combination still needs regimen-specific benefit and safety evidence.

points.entailment: pCR at surgery, individual prognosis, trial-level surrogacy and actually measured survival are distinct; a response gain is not a cure rate.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response at surgery, defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, and event-free survival from randomisation. The response definition permits residual in-situ disease in the breast while excluding invasive residual cancer in breast and nodes. Event-free survival counts progression preventing definitive surgery, local or distant recurrence, a second primary cancer or death from any cause; overall survival is a secondary endpoint counting death from any cause. Because death is part of EFS, it is an event rather than a competing event for that composite. Analysing a recurrence component alone can require a different competing-risk question.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The earlier adaptive phase 2 I-SPY2 report estimated pCR of 60% versus 22% in its triple-negative subgroup against its own chemotherapy control. That is a different comparison from KEYNOTE-522 and cannot establish a cross-trial treatment ranking. Likewise, better survival among people who achieve pCR is a prognostic association within selected response groups, not proof of the postoperative drug's separate effect or a validated rule selecting individual benefit. CTNeoBC found a strong pCR-outcome association but did not validate pCR as a trial-level surrogate for EFS or OS in its included trials. Here survival itself was measured.

points.heading: Try it
points.requirement: A friend says: "My tumor was PD-L1 negative, so pembrolizumab won't help me in early TNBC." What does the evidence say?

points.entailment: The 22C3/CPS and setting-specific advanced-TNBC threshold are separated from high-risk early-TNBC use without PD-L1 selection. The newer labelled sacituzumab regimen is explicitly separate from KEYNOTE-355; no marker predicts one person’s benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: KEYNOTE-355 studied 847 people with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In the PD-L1 combined-positive-score-at-least-10 subgroup, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 23.0 months versus 16.1 with placebo plus chemotherapy, with a death hazard ratio of 0.73. A median divides a study group in half; it is not an individual forecast. The October 2026 U.S. pembrolizumab label has no PD-L1 qualifier for its high-risk early-stage TNBC regimen, while its advanced TNBC indications with chemotherapy or sacituzumab govitecan specify CPS at least 10 and an FDA-authorised test. The sacituzumab combination is a separate labelled regimen, not the KEYNOTE-355 comparison. Population, regimen, scoring context and evidence must stay together.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The combined positive score is the number of PD-L1-staining tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages divided by the total number of viable tumour cells, multiplied by 100 (Cortes 2022). KEYNOTE-355 randomised 847 patients with untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer 2:1 to pembrolizumab or placebo with the investigator's chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine-carboplatin), with PD-L1 tested centrally by the 22C3 assay. Progression-free survival at the interim analysis was 9.7 against 5.6 months in the CPS 10 or more group (hazard ratio 0.65, primary objective met), 7.6 against 5.6 months in CPS 1 or more (0.74, not significant) and 7.5 against 5.6 months overall (0.82, not tested), the effect increasing with PD-L1 enrichment (Cortes 2020). At the final analysis (median follow-up 44.1 months) overall survival in the CPS 10 group was 23.0 against 16.1 months (hazard ratio 0.73, significant), 17.6 against 16.0 months in CPS 1 or more (0.86, not significant) and 17.2 against 15.5 months in all patients (0.89, not tested); grade 3 to 5 treatment-related events occurred in 68.1 against 66.9 percent (Cortes 2022). NICE recommends pembrolizumab with paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel for untreated triple-negative locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic breast cancer in the population the appraisal covers (TA801, June 2022). A different assay and score defined the earlier atezolizumab result: IMpassion130 used the SP142 immune-cell score with positivity at 1 percent or more of the tumour area; median progression-free survival was 7.5 against 5.0 months and overall survival 25.0 against 15.5 months in the PD-L1-positive subgroup, without a significant overall survival gain in the whole population (Schmid 2018), and the parent page's history records that approval was later withdrawn. Early disease needs no PD-L1 test: in KEYNOTE-522 pembrolizumab with chemotherapy raised pathological complete response from 51.2 to 64.8 percent in stage II and III disease unselected for PD-L1 (Schmid 2020) and five-year overall survival from 81.7 to 86.6 percent (Schmid 2024); NICE TA851 (December 2022) recommends it for triple-negative early or locally advanced breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. The biomarker readout pd-l1-cps carries the label wording for every CPS threshold across cancers.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The study question concerns the whole assigned sequence in previously untreated, non-metastatic stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer: T1c with N1 or N2, or T2 to T4 with N0 to N2, and performance status 0 or 1. The registry excludes prior checkpoint therapy and active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the preceding two years, among other criteria. There was one assignment of 784 people to pembrolizumab and 390 to placebo across preoperative chemotherapy, surgery and postoperative treatment, without a separate postoperative randomisation. Smaller node-negative tumours outside those entry criteria and metastatic disease are different settings. Entry did not require PD-L1 selection, and the high-risk early-stage indication in the prescribing information has no PD-L1 threshold.

points.heading: preamble
points.requirement: **T cells can recognize cancer, but tumors survive by hiding the target, keeping T cells out or switching them down. Checkpoint inhibitors release one of those brakes; in early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), adding one to chemotherapy improved survival.**

sourceRefs.exactPassage: **T cells can recognize cancer, but tumors survive by hiding the target, keeping T cells out or switching them down. Checkpoint inhibitors release one of those brakes; in early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), adding one to chemotherapy improved survival.**

**T cells can recognize cancer, but tumors survive by hiding the target, keeping T cells out or switching them down. Checkpoint inhibitors release one of those brakes; in early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), adding one to chemotherapy improved survival.**

points.entailment: Cancer-directed recognition, several escape dependencies and the tested early-TNBC chemotherapy-plus-checkpoint survival comparison retain population and mechanism scope.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Chen and Mellman’s 2013 framework describes seven linked steps: release of cancer antigens; their collection and presentation; T-cell priming and activation; trafficking; entry into tumour tissue; recognition of cancer cells; and killing. Further antigen release may support another round. In conventional T-cell recognition, a displayed peptide-HLA complex and a suitable T-cell receptor are separate dependencies.

This is a T-cell-centred organizing model, not a universal route, assay result or treatment-selection algorithm. Steps overlap, priming may occur away from the tumour, and other immune mechanisms require their own account. Checkpoints and local tissue conditions affect several steps. Vaccines aim to generate or expand reactive responses, checkpoint drugs interrupt selected inhibitory signals, and engineered cells provide a recognition system and effectors. Each still needs appropriate targets, access, function and safety evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Immune escape can involve loss of a targeted antigen, altered HLA alleles or processing, defective inducible signalling, inhibition after entry or impaired access. Anagnostou found loss of putative neoantigens in checkpoint-resistant lung tumours with accompanying T-cell evidence. McGranahan described allele-specific HLA loss in lung cancer evolution. Montesion’s commercial pan-cancer genomic series contained 83,644 samples with HLA-I loss of heterozygosity in 17%; this assay-defined pan-cancer observation is not a breast-specific prevalence. Allele loss differs from reversible expression change or a B2M defect affecting class-I surface display.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: KEYNOTE-522 randomised 1,174 people with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to pembrolizumab or placebo with chemotherapy before surgery, followed by continuation of the assigned antibody or placebo after surgery. At a median follow-up of 75.1 months, estimated 60-month overall survival was 86.6 per cent versus 81.7 per cent. Enrolment did not require PD-L1 positivity. The trial compared the whole perioperative regimen and was not designed to isolate the contribution of each treatment phase. These group results do not predict one person's outcome.

points.heading: The big ideas
points.requirement: 1. **A T cell sees a fragment, not a whole cell.** It recognizes a short protein piece displayed on [human leukocyte antigen (HLA)](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antigen-presentation/hla). No display, no recognition.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: 1. **A T cell sees a fragment, not a whole cell.** It recognizes a short protein piece displayed on [human leukocyte antigen (HLA)](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antigen-presentation/hla). No display, no recognition.

1. **A T cell sees a fragment, not a whole cell.** It recognizes a short protein piece displayed on [human leukocyte antigen (HLA)](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antigen-presentation/hla). No display, no recognition.

points.entailment: The fragment/HLA requirement is scoped to conventional alpha-beta recognition rather than every possible T-cell family.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: T cells develop through the thymus. Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognise peptide-HLA displays through a paired receptor; CD4 and CD8 identify major co-receptor populations, rather than fixed helper and killer jobs. Some human bladder-tumour CD4 cells showed class-II-dependent cytotoxicity in controlled experiments, while regulatory populations restrain responses. Identity, receptor specificity, state and measured function need separate evidence. A CD3 or CD8 stain establishes a sampled population under a defined panel, not tumour recognition or killing. Report compartment, viable-cell denominator, marker panel and timing. Controlled recognition and target-cell-death assays address different claims; cytokine production, division and treatment benefit are also separate outcomes.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: For a coding change to supply a conventional T-cell target, its information must be expressed, protein produced and processed into a fragment, that peptide displayed with HLA, and a suitable receptor able to recognise the display. DNA, RNA, protein, recovered displayed peptide and controlled recognition are separate observations. A prediction at one step does not measure all the others. This conventional alpha-beta route does not describe every T cell, antibody or natural killer recognition system.

points.heading: The big ideas
points.requirement: 2. **Starting a response takes more than recognition.** Dendritic cells must carry the fragment to a lymph node and supply supporting signals.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: 2. **Starting a response takes more than recognition.** Dendritic cells must carry the fragment to a lymph node and supply supporting signals.

points.entailment: Recognition/priming and access are separate; soluble antigen can reach resident presenters, and neither courier-to-node nor blood-vessel route is a universal itinerary.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Identity and state are different questions. Immature and mature describe response-related states, and maturation can change antigen handling, costimulation, cytokines and movement without turning one subset into another. Presentation can support tolerance as well as activation, so antigen uptake, mature-looking markers and functional priming are separate observations. Where cells meet also matters. Some dendritic cells carry antigen from tissue to a draining lymph node, while resident cells in the node take up soluble antigen that arrives in lymph through conduits before migrating cells arrive (Sixt et al., 2005, mouse). In mouse tumours, cDC1 accumulation often depended on natural killer cells that produced the chemokines CCL5 and XCL1, tumour prostaglandin E2 disrupted that axis, and in human cancers the same transcripts tracked natural killer and cDC1 signatures and were associated with longer overall survival, an association (Böttcher et al., 2018).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Three limits matter for tumours. A vaccine that reaches a dendritic cell may make the encoded protein inside it, and that class I display need not be cross-presentation. A dendritic cell can supply a priming opportunity, but the cancer cell must itself display a recognisable target for an antigen-specific CD8 T cell to attack it, so successful presentation does not repair a cancer cell's loss of an HLA allele. And a low count in one biopsy does not show that no priming happened in another compartment. Subsets are identified by flow cytometry, tissue staining, spatial and RNA methods, but whether a cell presents a defined target and stimulates a suitable responder needs a functional test with controls.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Lymph drains fluid from tissues back to the blood, passing through nodes where T and B cells inspect it for infection; cancer cells that enter lymph vessels lodge in the nearest nodes first, so node involvement (the N in TNM) is a central marker of a cancer's tendency to spread and raises the stage. Sentinel-node biopsy identifies and removes only the first node or two that drain a tumour, sparing patients the arm swelling (lymphoedema) that removing all nodes causes. Lymph nodes are also where immune responses against a tumour are launched, and where immunotherapy needs functioning T cells to be primed. Afferent vessels bring lymph into a node and efferent vessels carry it out, and a draining node names a route and not a finding of cancer. Immune material and cells reach a node by different routes: soluble antigen can reach resident dendritic cells through conduits in the node before migrating dendritic cells arrive (Sixt et al., 2005, mouse), while lymphocytes are recruited from the blood through high endothelial venules (Brulois et al., 2020, mouse). Lymph is interstitial fluid collected by lymph capillaries and returned to the venous blood (National Cancer Institute SEER training), so lymph and blood are different fluids and a sample of one does not stand in for the other. A tertiary lymphoid structure is an ectopic lymphoid aggregate that forms in tissue such as a tumour, and it is not a lymph node (Schumacher and Thommen, 2022). Size on imaging is a measurement in millimetres and not a finding of cancer or priming, and a report should say which node was measured, by what method and when (OnCo reporting advice). A node has a cortex, a paracortex and a medulla, and B cells and T cells home to separate areas within them (Willard-Mack, 2006); in the mouse, a venous population in the medulla was predicted to recruit myeloid cells rather than lymphocytes, which videomicroscopy confirmed (Brulois et al., 2020). In gene-targeted mice, loss of the chemokine receptor CCR7 altered the organisation of lymphoid organs and stopped skin dendritic cells reaching draining nodes (Förster et al., 1999). Arrival of material in a node does not show that priming succeeded. Pathological involvement means cancer was identified in examined tissue, which differs from a drainage route, enlargement or an imaging observation, and a negative sampled node does not certify the unsampled nodes (the National Cancer Institute notes that a false-negative biopsy gives a false sense of security about the extent of cancer).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Priming is a naive cell's initial activation in a supporting context. Signal one is TCR recognition of peptide-HLA, signal two includes CD80/CD86-CD28 costimulation and inhibitory context, and signal three includes differentiation-supporting cytokines. The receptor pre-exists the encounter. These signals interact over time; the model is not a three-button checklist and antigen-experienced or engineered cells can have different requirements.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A common blood-borne effector route separates recruitment from vessel entry, movement through stroma and contact with relevant cancer cells. Rolling, firm adhesion and passage across vessel lining are distinct steps; in the melanoma transfer models, CXCR3 loss impaired firm arrest and extravasation without preventing initial rolling. This does not establish the itinerary or chemokine dependence of every resident T cell. A cell can inspect peptide-HLA on other cells along the way, so entering a cancer-cell nest is not the first possible recognition event.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Immune surveillance concerns immune control of transformed cells. Immunoediting adds that immune pressure can alter which cancer populations persist. Shankaran’s genetically defined mouse experiments support lymphocyte and interferon-gamma contributions to control and selection. They do not measure what fraction of all human cancers immunity prevents.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: CTLA-4 is often emphasised during priming in lymphoid sites and PD-1 during ongoing responses in tissues. LAG-3, TIM-3 and TIGIT have their own biology rather than being interchangeable versions of PD-1. A regulator identified in an experimental model does not establish benefit from blocking it in another population; each intervention needs its own evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Checkpoint blockade changes an inhibitory interaction; it does not install a new recognition receptor or reconstruct required HLA machinery that has been genetically lost. Vaccines, engineered cell receptors and cytokines change different inputs, and a plausible combination still needs regimen-specific benefit and safety evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Chen and Mellman’s 2013 framework describes seven linked steps: release of cancer antigens; their collection and presentation; T-cell priming and activation; trafficking; entry into tumour tissue; recognition of cancer cells; and killing. Further antigen release may support another round. In conventional T-cell recognition, a displayed peptide-HLA complex and a suitable T-cell receptor are separate dependencies.

This is a T-cell-centred organizing model, not a universal route, assay result or treatment-selection algorithm. Steps overlap, priming may occur away from the tumour, and other immune mechanisms require their own account. Checkpoints and local tissue conditions affect several steps. Vaccines aim to generate or expand reactive responses, checkpoint drugs interrupt selected inhibitory signals, and engineered cells provide a recognition system and effectors. Each still needs appropriate targets, access, function and safety evidence.

points.requirement: A tumor sample is full of T cells and stains PD-L1-positive. Why is that encouraging, and what is still open?

points.entailment: The fictional T-cell-rich/PD-L1-positive sample supports distribution and measured expression, not proof of cancer specificity, complete display, induced feedback or added drug benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A PD-L1 stain measures protein on defined tumour and immune cells, not why it is present. Colocalization with lymphocytes and interferon-related expression can support induced expression, while a uniform lymphocyte-poor pattern raises other hypotheses; neither pattern proves a cause. Adding interferon gamma and measuring PD-L1 tests inducibility in a laboratory model. Appropriate pathway perturbations and controls investigate causation, and neither that assay nor a tissue score measures the entire in-vivo feedback loop or treatment benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

These are observations about identity and location. Some infiltrating T cells recognize viral or other non-cancer antigens; others restrain responses. Region, specimen, disease site and sampling time matter, and treatment can change the pattern. Neither a small biopsy nor a pattern label describes every site in a person or selects an immunotherapy. Exclusion suggests questions about recruitment, vessels, matrix and local cells, rather than proving one causal wall.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: KEYNOTE-355 studied 847 people with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In the PD-L1 combined-positive-score-at-least-10 subgroup, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 23.0 months versus 16.1 with placebo plus chemotherapy, with a death hazard ratio of 0.73. A median divides a study group in half; it is not an individual forecast. The October 2026 U.S. pembrolizumab label has no PD-L1 qualifier for its high-risk early-stage TNBC regimen, while its advanced TNBC indications with chemotherapy or sacituzumab govitecan specify CPS at least 10 and an FDA-authorised test. The sacituzumab combination is a separate labelled regimen, not the KEYNOTE-355 comparison. Population, regimen, scoring context and evidence must stay together.

points.heading: Check your understanding
points.requirement: **Explain it back:** "To explain an immune treatment, I name what it recognizes, which step it changes and which trial shows an effect."

sourceRefs.exactPassage: **Explain it back:** "To explain an immune treatment, I name what it recognizes, which step it changes and which trial shows an effect."

points.entailment: The explanation rule names recognition requirement, measured intervention step and population-specific comparative evidence; it is not a personal treatment algorithm.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: An immune observation suggests a question ladder: identify the cells and their location; ask whether a proposed peptide is produced and displayed; test recognition against appropriate target and background controls; distinguish tissue entry from useful target-specific function; then seek clinical comparisons for benefit and harm. Poor display, few matching cells, failed tissue access and impaired local function are different proposed failures. A count, supplied-peptide response or plausible pathway alone cannot complete that chain. These are task-dependent interpretation questions, not a mandatory clinical test menu.

points.heading: What is still uncertain
points.requirement: - Whether checkpoint benefit in early TNBC comes from the treatment before surgery, after it, or both; KEYNOTE-522 was not designed to separate them.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: - Whether checkpoint benefit in early TNBC comes from the treatment before surgery, after it, or both; KEYNOTE-522 was not designed to separate them.

points.entailment: The trial compared the complete perioperative sequence and did not isolate the preoperative/postoperative contribution; the additional perioperative link itself is routing.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The study question concerns the whole assigned sequence in previously untreated, non-metastatic stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer: T1c with N1 or N2, or T2 to T4 with N0 to N2, and performance status 0 or 1. The registry excludes prior checkpoint therapy and active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the preceding two years, among other criteria. There was one assignment of 784 people to pembrolizumab and 390 to placebo across preoperative chemotherapy, surgery and postoperative treatment, without a separate postoperative randomisation. Smaller node-negative tumours outside those entry criteria and metastatic disease are different settings. Entry did not require PD-L1 selection, and the high-risk early-stage indication in the prescribing information has no PD-L1 threshold.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The postoperative-only question remains distinct: OptimICE-pCR randomises people after pCR to postoperative pembrolizumab or observation, and the registry lists it as recruiting with no posted results. KEYNOTE-522 did not randomise dropping a chemotherapy component. CREATE-X compared postoperative capecitabine with standard postsurgical treatment after residual HER2-negative disease, while OlympiA compared olaparib with placebo in eligible high-risk germline BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative disease after chemotherapy and local treatment. Those reports describe their own comparisons rather than a randomised test of adding either drug to the KEYNOTE-522 sequence. No result here is a personal forecast or a treatment-omission rule.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In chronic LCMV infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor exhausted cells self-renewed and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-L1 blockade. In Miller's mouse tumour experiments, progenitor cells persisted and expanded after PD-1 blockade, whereas terminally exhausted cells had greater immediate cytotoxicity against tested tumour targets. Persistence, capacity to divide after restimulation and immediate killing are different functions. The human melanoma component associated progenitor-like features with outcomes; it was not a universal predictive test, and terminally exhausted does not mean inert.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Paired human basal-cell and squamous-cell skin-cancer biopsies after anti-PD-1 showed expanded clonotypes not previously observed in the same tumour. Clonal replacement and reinvigoration of resident cells are different, potentially overlapping response explanations. Non-detection before therapy is not proof of whole-body absence. Breast-cancer single-cell work identified checkpoint/effector-rich tissue-resident CD8 populations; its early TNBC survival signature was an association, not a general treatment predictor.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) is the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) system, with two main classes of peptide-display molecule. Classical class I (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C) has a heavy chain, beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a bound peptide, is found on most nucleated cells, usually displays peptides from proteins made inside the cell and is read by CD8 T cells. Class II (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ) has alpha and beta chains with a bound peptide, is mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (expression can be induced elsewhere), usually displays proteins processed in vesicles, often acquired from outside, and is read by CD4 T cells. These are common routes, not exclusive lists: cross-presentation puts externally acquired antigen on class I without making it class II, and a CD4 response is not proof of matching class I tumour display. CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors and usual recognition partners, not guarantees of cell function. Structural work shows the T-cell receptor lying across the peptide and HLA together (Garboczi et al., 1996), CD8 contacting the class I alpha2 and alpha3 domains and B2M (Gao et al., 1997) and CD4 engaging a separate class II region (Yin et al., 2012); these constructs do not define universal angles or functions.

HLA alleles are shared across people, and a person inherits a combination that is not necessarily unique. Each person inherits two copies each of HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C, so a cell can display up to six classical class I variants at once. The IPD-IMGT/HLA statistics page read on 9 November 2026 listed 46,146 HLA alleles, 31,311 class I and 14,835 class II (9,457 HLA-A, 11,328 HLA-B and 9,580 HLA-C alleles). Binding predictors estimate whether a peptide can fit a specified allele's groove, but processing, transport, loading and surface expression decide whether it is displayed. Sarkizova et al. (2020) profiled more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 mono-allelic cell lines to learn allele-specific motifs and build prediction models; that is allele-level data, not proof of any cell's display. Kaur et al. (2017) showed that HLA-C surface expression varies across individuals in an allele-specific manner, influenced by the structure of the peptide-binding cleft and peptide diversity; Apps and colleagues found lower HLA-C than HLA-A/B in the analysed healthy-donor peripheral blood lymphocytes with the A*02:01/B*44:02/C*05:01 haplotype; the magnitude differed between flow cytometry and mass spectrometry. This is a defined comparison, not a universal hierarchy. The small HLA-C peptide share observed by Schellens and colleagues in four B lymphoblastoid cell lines was also affected by their assignment method, which gave HLA-A/B precedence; it is not a universal biological fraction.

In cancer, class I HLA shows peptides to CD8 T cells and is also the main ligand for inhibitory receptors on natural killer cells, so losing it can hide a tumour from T cells while removing a brake on NK cells. HLA-E and HLA-G are nonclassical and vary little between people; HLA-E presents leader peptides from other class I molecules and binds the NK receptor CD94/NKG2A (Braud et al., 1998, with HLA-E tetramers). Tumours can lose a presenting allele (HLA loss of heterozygosity), alter processing or reduce expression, and allele-specific loss differs from complete loss of conventional class I display; targets on retained alleles may remain possible. Tran et al. (2016) documented a colorectal cancer lesion that progressed after T-cell therapy against mutant KRAS G12D, which had lost the chromosome 6 haplotype encoding the restricting HLA-C*08:02; this shows escape in one patient, not a rate. Typing, protein expression, recovered peptide, recognition and killing are different observations, and a conventional surface-target engager avoids peptide-HLA dependence while a peptide-HLA-directed engager keeps it.

B2M is the light chain of classical class I and does not span the membrane; class II contains no B2M, so CD4 T-cell recognition can remain when B2M is lost. B2M also partners other class I-like molecules: UniProt records heterotrimers with HLA-E, HLA-G, HLA-F and MR1 and lists CD1 interactions, and a B2M mutation caused deficiency of the neonatal Fc receptor FcRn in two siblings (Wani et al., 2006), so complete B2M loss can remove more than classical class I. Loss of one HLA allele can leave other presenting alleles usable, whereas loss of functional B2M impairs many class I targets at once, so several peptides on different alleles are not independent protection. A B2M variant, low RNA, absent surface class I and a blood B2M concentration are different observations: one variant does not show complete functional loss, and blood B2M does not count tumour peptide-HLA complexes. Zaretsky et al. (2016) linked a truncating B2M mutation to lost surface class I in one melanoma relapse after PD-1 blockade, which is a mechanism in that setting, not a frequency. Reduced class I display does not guarantee NK-cell killing, because activating signals are still needed.

points.heading: Recognition is a three-part contact
points.requirement: Most conventional T cells use a receptor made from an alpha and a beta chain. The receptor contacts both the peptide and its human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecule. The receptor works with CD3 signaling proteins and, often, a [CD4 or CD8 co-receptor](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/t-cells/cd4-vs-cd8).

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Antigen-processing machinery (APM) is the set of proteins that generate, transport and load peptides onto HLA. A common class I route has five steps. (1) The proteasome cuts intracellular proteins into fragments, which can create a useful peptide or destroy it. (2) The transporter associated with antigen processing, TAP1 with TAP2, moves peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum; Shepherd et al. (1993) showed in a cell-free system that TAP1 is part of an ATP-dependent, sequence-selective peptide translocator. (3) ERAP1 and ERAP2 trim amino acids from the front end. York et al. (2002) found that ERAP1 can enhance or limit presentation by trimming epitopes to 8 to 9 residues, and Saveanu et al. (2005) found complementary human ERAP1 and ERAP2 activity, so more expression does not universally improve display. A class I HLA heavy chain assembles with beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a peptide, with helpers such as tapasin. (4) Stable peptide-HLA complexes reach the surface; the peptide stays held by HLA. (5) A compatible T-cell receptor on a conventional CD8 T cell may recognise the pair; recognition is a separate gate and display alone does not show killing.

Class II HLA commonly loads peptides in vesicles that process acquired proteins. An invariant chain protects the new groove and directs it there; after cutting, a remaining fragment is exchanged for other peptides with help from HLA-DM, and conventional CD4 T cells inspect these displays. Cross-presentation lets externally acquired material reach class I. The scheme is a common route, not a rule for every peptide.

A cancer cell may keep an altered protein and still show little of its peptide, and a shared processing defect can affect several targets at once, so adding candidate peptides does not bypass the bottleneck. Low expression, gene loss and a functional defect are different findings: a weak RNA signal does not prove deletion. Interferon gamma can increase presentation machinery when its signalling pathway and the required genes are intact, and cannot replace a deleted B2M or HLA gene. Sucker et al. Peptide loading can bypass processing, so rescue by supplied peptide supports a bottleneck under those conditions only. Binding prediction is not presentation, and CD4 help is not proof of CD8 tumour recognition.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Antigen-processing machinery (APM) is the set of proteins that generate, transport and load peptides onto HLA. A common class I route has five steps. (1) The proteasome cuts intracellular proteins into fragments, which can create a useful peptide or destroy it. (2) The transporter associated with antigen processing, TAP1 with TAP2, moves peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum; Shepherd et al. (1993) showed in a cell-free system that TAP1 is part of an ATP-dependent, sequence-selective peptide translocator. (3) ERAP1 and ERAP2 trim amino acids from the front end. York et al. (2002) found that ERAP1 can enhance or limit presentation by trimming epitopes to 8 to 9 residues, and Saveanu et al. (2005) found complementary human ERAP1 and ERAP2 activity, so more expression does not universally improve display. A class I HLA heavy chain assembles with beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a peptide, with helpers such as tapasin. (4) Stable peptide-HLA complexes reach the surface; the peptide stays held by HLA. (5) A compatible T-cell receptor on a conventional CD8 T cell may recognise the pair; recognition is a separate gate and display alone does not show killing.

Class II HLA commonly loads peptides in vesicles that process acquired proteins. An invariant chain protects the new groove and directs it there; after cutting, a remaining fragment is exchanged for other peptides with help from HLA-DM, and conventional CD4 T cells inspect these displays. Cross-presentation lets externally acquired material reach class I. The scheme is a common route, not a rule for every peptide.

These are melanoma observations, not treatment-benefit evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Human studies support continued thymic output into adulthood, with age-related decline rather than a fixed birthday shutdown. Existing naive cells can also survive and divide outside the thymus. Human and mouse kinetic studies found different contributions of thymic output and peripheral division; mouse dependence on new output cannot be transferred directly to adult humans.

T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are rearrangement by-products that do not replicate with chromosomes. Peripheral division can dilute measured TREC content. In a fictional closed ledger, 2 cells carrying 4 total circles divide into 4 cells retaining 4 circles: average copies per cell fall from 2 to 1. Allocation can be uneven. This isolates division and does not count new arrivals or daily thymic export. Copies per cell and copies per blood volume have different denominators. Interpret output with survival, division, movement, compartment and timing; naive phenotype, thymic imaging or TREC content alone cannot provide a complete immune-age or cancer-benefit forecast.

points.entailment: Bulk versus compatible paired single-cell/phenotype methods, nucleic-acid input and amount, chain/grouping rule, transcript/amplification effects and rare-clone sampling limits retain distinct meanings. Read counts are not automatically cells.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Assay card: measures receptor identities, usually by the complementarity-determining region 3 of the variable region, and their measured representation in the sampled population. How: extract nucleic acid, amplify or capture receptor regions, sequence, then group and count under stated rules, which may use nucleotide or amino-acid sequence, gene segments, one chain or paired chains. Input: blood cells or tissue nucleic acid for bulk methods and compatible cell preparations for single-cell methods, and preparation consumes material. A high-resolution human repertoire method reported chain diversity without sequence-associated or quantitative restrictions (Ruggiero 2015). Failure modes: poor material, shallow sampling, amplification bias, chain mismatch, inconsistent definitions and batch effects. It cannot tell every receptor's target, tissue position, killing or benefit, and a research method is not automatically a treatment-selection test.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Nucleotide and amino-acid clonotypes need not be the same grouping. The standard genetic code assigns several codons to the same amino acid, so different nucleotide sequences can encode the same receptor segment; amino-acid identity alone is not proof of one cellular lineage. MIGEC introduced molecular-identifier groups to correct PCR and sequencing errors in antibody and T-cell receptor repertoire profiling (Shugay 2014). Such error correction does not restore molecules absent from the sample. Report which chain, grouping rule and abundance unit the method actually used.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

A sequence found in dissociated tumour material does not locate its cell inside a cancer-cell nest. B changes from 3.0% to 3.1% and is not detected in that tumour sample. A is a candidate, while neither the large B share nor overlap for A identifies an antigen. If a separate mixed-cell peptide assay is positive, it has not assigned that response to A. Link the same cells and compatible paired alpha-beta receptor to a controlled peptide-HLA response, then test naturally presenting targets, killing and cross-reactivity. Relative frequency is not absolute cell expansion, and non-detection in one sample is not whole-body absence.

points.heading: A worked example
points.requirement: Invented numbers for learning: a clone rises from 0.1% to 2% of sampled blood receptors after vaccination. That is relative enrichment in those samples. It does not alone prove absolute expansion: other clones could have declined. Compatible cell counts, sampling and assay denominators are needed for the absolute-number claim. [Clonality metrics](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/immune-monitoring/tcr-clonality-metrics) describe the distribution. A paired functional assay against the intended peptide can strengthen a specificity claim. Tumor-cell killing and clinical benefit require further evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Yee, Lizee and Schueneman describe three ways of adoptive T-cell transfer: tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes taken from a biopsy; lymphocytes redirected by a chimeric antigen receptor or T-cell receptor; and the isolation and expansion of often low-frequency endogenous T cells reactive to tumour antigens from the peripheral blood, which they call endogenous T-cell (ETC) therapy (Cancer Journal 2015). It needs specialised methods to isolate and expand very low-frequency tumour-reactive T cells from blood, and the authors note that a trial can be started quickly once a tumour-associated target epitope has been identified (Cancer Journal 2015). The early melanoma trials at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center infused such cells as clones against MART-1, gp100, tyrosinase and NY-ESO-1.

Same-cell compatible alpha-beta linkage and controlled peptide-HLA response remain necessary, with natural tumour killing, cross-reactivity and benefit separate.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Hormones, growth factors and other molecules can bind receptors, but ligand describes the interaction rather than one functional effect. A bound ligand may activate a specified response, oppose another ligand, or show no effect in that assay. Some targeting ligands localize a payload. An accessible binding address need not be a cancer’s growth driver; delivery, intracellular action and clinical benefit require further evidence.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In an invented comparison, a plain antibody binds surface protein A, the same binder carrying a payload damages tested cells, and a blocker lowers an internal signal. These establish different measured outcomes: accessible binding, activity of the finished construct, and an effect on the specified pathway. None alone establishes tumour dependence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit. Ask what binds what, what changes and which experiment measured the change; a shared address does not supply a shared action.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A typical IgG has two antigen-binding arms; receptor binding and cross-reactivity depend on the particular molecule and test system, while its stem (the Fc region) can recruit immune cells and complement or extend the antibody's life in the blood. Therapeutic antibodies block growth receptors (trastuzumab on HER2, cetuximab on EGFR), release the brakes on T cells (pembrolizumab on PD-1), flag cancer cells for immune killing (rituximab on CD20), or serve as the targeting vehicle of ADCs and radioimmunotherapy. Bispecific formats have two binding specificities. Some are designed to bring a T cell and a target cell together; their structures and functions vary. Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement. Antibodies that bind the same target can act differently: a blocking antibody, an antibody-drug conjugate and a bispecific format can share a target and still differ in what follows.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A typical IgG has two antigen-binding arms; receptor binding and cross-reactivity depend on the particular molecule and test system, while its stem (the Fc region) can recruit immune cells and complement or extend the antibody's life in the blood. Therapeutic antibodies block growth receptors (trastuzumab on HER2, cetuximab on EGFR), release the brakes on T cells (pembrolizumab on PD-1), flag cancer cells for immune killing (rituximab on CD20), or serve as the targeting vehicle of ADCs and radioimmunotherapy. Bispecific formats have two binding specificities. Some are designed to bring a T cell and a target cell together; their structures and functions vary. Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement. Antibodies that bind the same target can act differently: a blocking antibody, an antibody-drug conjugate and a bispecific format can share a target and still differ in what follows.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Receptors can be on the surface or inside a cell. Ligand-gated ion channels regulate ion passage; G-protein-coupled receptors act through G proteins; enzyme-linked receptors can contain an enzyme or recruit a separate one. Intracellular nuclear receptors can regulate transcription with cellular partners. A surface signal can ultimately alter genes, while nuclear-receptor family membership does not fix every molecule permanently in the nucleus or require every effect to use new transcription.

points.heading: preamble
points.requirement: **Displaying a target and starting a useful T-cell response are different jobs. [Dendritic cells](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/innate-and-unconventional-cells/dendritic-cells) help connect them.**

sourceRefs.exactPassage: **Displaying a target and starting a useful T-cell response are different jobs. [Dendritic cells](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/innate-and-unconventional-cells/dendritic-cells) help connect them.**

**Displaying a target and starting a useful T-cell response are different jobs. [Dendritic cells](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/innate-and-unconventional-cells/dendritic-cells) help connect them.**

points.entailment: Dendritic acquisition/display, supporting context and naive initial activation remain distinct. The naive receptor pre-exists; a displayed cancer-cell target is not proof of efficient priming, and one biopsy cannot exclude priming elsewhere.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Dendritic cells acquire material from their surroundings or make antigen themselves, process proteins and display fragments on HLA molecules, where a matching T-cell receptor can recognise a peptide and HLA pair. Cross-presentation is the route that places acquired material on class I, and class II presentation, usually of acquired proteins to CD4 T cells, is a separate route. They are a family of subsets with overlapping jobs. Conventional type 1 cells (cDC1) are particularly important for cross-presentation: mice lacking the transcription factor Batf3 lost CD8-alpha-positive dendritic cells, their dendritic cells were defective in cross-presentation, and they rejected highly immunogenic tumours less well (Hildner et al., 2008). Human CD141-positive dendritic cells, activated with poly I:C, cross-presented soluble antigen and antigen from necrotic virus-infected cells better than CD1c-positive cells (Jongbloed et al., 2010). Conventional type 2 cells are usually studied for class II presentation to CD4 T cells, and plasmacytoid cells for type I interferon responses. In a review, plasmacytoid cells are described as producing large amounts of interferon alpha, while the contribution of CD11b-positive conventional cells to CD4 T-cell priming in vivo was still described as to be determined (Merad et al., 2013). The same review describes conventional cells as inducing immunity to foreign antigens and enforcing tolerance to self-antigens, and migration-linked maturation as raising MHC class II and costimulatory molecules, with cytokine production added when migration follows inflammation. In mice, antigen delivered to dendritic cells in the steady state led to brief T-cell activation followed by loss and unresponsiveness of the T cells, and adding an anti-CD40 antibody changed the outcome to prolonged activation (Hawiger et al., 2001). For conventional type 2 cells, a review of dendritic cells in T-cell programming reported that they were most often found to be required for CD4 T-cell priming in mice, with T helper 1 differentiation as an exception in which type 1 cells were often required, and noted that type 2 cells can be difficult to distinguish from monocyte-derived cells because markers overlap (Eisenbarth, 2019); another review said that specific depletion of type 2 cells was still needed to confirm their unique role in priming CD4 T cells (Durai and Murphy, 2016). Single-cell sequencing of human blood found six dendritic-cell and four monocyte subtypes, including a population that resembles plasmacytoid cells but potently activates T cells, so one positive marker is weaker evidence than a supported subset assignment (Villani et al., 2017).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Identity and state are different questions. Immature and mature describe response-related states, and maturation can change antigen handling, costimulation, cytokines and movement without turning one subset into another. Presentation can support tolerance as well as activation, so antigen uptake, mature-looking markers and functional priming are separate observations. Where cells meet also matters. Some dendritic cells carry antigen from tissue to a draining lymph node, while resident cells in the node take up soluble antigen that arrives in lymph through conduits before migrating cells arrive (Sixt et al., 2005, mouse). In mouse tumours, cDC1 accumulation often depended on natural killer cells that produced the chemokines CCL5 and XCL1, tumour prostaglandin E2 disrupted that axis, and in human cancers the same transcripts tracked natural killer and cDC1 signatures and were associated with longer overall survival, an association (Böttcher et al., 2018).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Three limits matter for tumours. A vaccine that reaches a dendritic cell may make the encoded protein inside it, and that class I display need not be cross-presentation. A dendritic cell can supply a priming opportunity, but the cancer cell must itself display a recognisable target for an antigen-specific CD8 T cell to attack it, so successful presentation does not repair a cancer cell's loss of an HLA allele. And a low count in one biopsy does not show that no priming happened in another compartment. Subsets are identified by flow cytometry, tissue staining, spatial and RNA methods, but whether a cell presents a defined target and stimulates a suitable responder needs a functional test with controls.
