anchors.text: PD-1 can accompany activation as well as exhaustion. TCF1 also occurs in naive and memory contexts. TIM-3/CD39, TOX and residency-associated CD103/CD39 require population and assay context; no single marker assigns state or specificity. Combine compatible response history, protein or RNA programmes, receptor identities and controlled function. TOX may be measured by intracellular staining or RNA; this is not a routine universal pathology classifier.

anchors.text: Paired human basal-cell and squamous-cell skin-cancer biopsies after anti-PD-1 showed expanded clonotypes not previously observed in the same tumour. Clonal replacement and reinvigoration of resident cells are different, potentially overlapping response explanations. Non-detection before therapy is not proof of whole-body absence. Breast-cancer single-cell work identified checkpoint/effector-rich tissue-resident CD8 populations; its early TNBC survival signature was an association, not a general treatment predictor.

anchors.text: In chronic LCMV infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor exhausted cells self-renewed and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-L1 blockade. In Miller's mouse tumour experiments, progenitor cells persisted and expanded after PD-1 blockade, whereas terminally exhausted cells had greater immediate cytotoxicity against tested tumour targets. Persistence, capacity to divide after restimulation and immediate killing are different functions. The human melanoma component associated progenitor-like features with outcomes; it was not a universal predictive test, and terminally exhausted does not mean inert.

anchors.text: The same paired receptor can occur with different functional phenotypes and response histories. Fictional R1 memory-associated and progenitor-like exhausted observations are separate observations, not a measured transition. Progenitor-like exhaustion is distinct from ordinary memory; shared TCF1 or division does not make their programmes equivalent.

anchors.text:
Human studies support continued thymic output into adulthood, with age-related decline rather than a fixed birthday shutdown. Existing naive cells can also survive and divide outside the thymus. Human and mouse kinetic studies found different contributions of thymic output and peripheral division; mouse dependence on new output cannot be transferred directly to adult humans.

T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are rearrangement by-products that do not replicate with chromosomes. Peripheral division can dilute measured TREC content. In a fictional closed ledger, 2 cells carrying 4 total circles divide into 4 cells retaining 4 circles: average copies per cell fall from 2 to 1. Allocation can be uneven. This isolates division and does not count new arrivals or daily thymic export. Copies per cell and copies per blood volume have different denominators. Interpret output with survival, division, movement, compartment and timing; naive phenotype, thymic imaging or TREC content alone cannot provide a complete immune-age or cancer-benefit forecast.

anchors.text: Thymic output is release of newly developed T cells; involution is a gradual, variable decline in active tissue rather than a fixed adult-age shutdown. Human age and HIV-treatment measurements support adult output, but no universal individual output rate. Naive-cell maintenance also reflects survival, peripheral division, movement and loss. Human/mouse kinetic comparisons found materially different dependencies; mouse output cannot dictate a human collection or banking rule.

anchors.text: Naive phenotype is not a recent-emigrant birth certificate. Flow phenotype/counts, kinetic labelling and modelling, receptor sequencing and thymic imaging supply different information; imaging is not a direct daily output count. Interpret measurements with exposure, compartment, observation time, division, survival and movement. Neither more diversity, adult output nor age alone promises a new cancer-recognising receptor, vaccine benefit or a collection recommendation.

anchors.text: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

anchors.text: The original peptide-MHC tetramer study made soluble multimeric peptide-display complexes to identify antigen-specific T cells. Binding correlated with cytotoxicity in the tested systems, but those observations are different measurements. The chosen peptide and HLA molecule define which interaction is tested. Detecting multimer-binding cells does not by itself establish natural display of that peptide by a tumor, successful target-cell killing or a clinical treatment effect.

anchors.text: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

anchors.text: The original enzyme-linked immunospot method counted antibody-secreting cells; cytokine versions are used to examine stimulated immune-cell responses. Cancer Vaccine Consortium proficiency panels showed that sample handling, protocol choices and plate reading affected results. A result needs the measured molecule, stimulation, cell input, background and reporting rule. A positive secretion response alone does not show that the sampled cells recognize or kill an unmodified tumor.

anchors.text: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

anchors.text: In a fictional population of 100 cancer cells, 80 display target X and 20 do not. Killing the X-positive 80 leaves 20 survivors; ten times as many effector cells does not create X on them. For two targets, suppose 20 cells carry both X and Y, 60 carry X only, ten Y only and ten neither. An idealised either-target rule covers 90 cells, whereas a both-target rule covers 20. These are recognition-coverage calculations, not measured killing or healthy-tissue selectivity. Expression thresholds, tissue access and cell function still matter.

anchors.text: Kawalekar’s defined human-CAR experiments linked 4-1BB signalling to outgrowth of CD8 central-memory cells with greater respiratory capacity, fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis. CD28-containing CARs produced effector-memory cells with a gene-expression pattern consistent with greater glycolysis. These are construct-and-system observations, not a ranking of clinical speed, persistence or safety by domain name. Other receptor parts, preparation, starting-cell state, target and disease setting remain relevant. Ramos simultaneously infused separately tracked second- and third-generation products. Their different expansion and persistence did not let a shared tumour response isolate either product’s clinical contribution.

anchors.text: Immune escape can involve loss of a targeted antigen, altered HLA alleles or processing, defective inducible signalling, inhibition after entry or impaired access. Anagnostou found loss of putative neoantigens in checkpoint-resistant lung tumours with accompanying T-cell evidence. McGranahan described allele-specific HLA loss in lung cancer evolution. Montesion’s commercial pan-cancer genomic series contained 83,644 samples with HLA-I loss of heterozygosity in 17%; this assay-defined pan-cancer observation is not a breast-specific prevalence. Allele loss differs from reversible expression change or a B2M defect affecting class-I surface display.

anchors.text: Treatment can select a pre-existing population and new changes can arise. Earlier specimens, retained alleles, expression, stimulation and controlled functional comparisons help test an escape explanation. Different sites may have different bottlenecks; several mechanisms may coexist. Blood tumour DNA alone does not identify a particular escape route. A proposed HLA-independent recognizer or combination still needs its own target, access, function and safety evidence, and a restored laboratory endpoint does not establish clinical benefit.

anchors.text: An immune observation suggests a question ladder: identify the cells and their location; ask whether a proposed peptide is produced and displayed; test recognition against appropriate target and background controls; distinguish tissue entry from useful target-specific function; then seek clinical comparisons for benefit and harm. Poor display, few matching cells, failed tissue access and impaired local function are different proposed failures. A count, supplied-peptide response or plausible pathway alone cannot complete that chain. These are task-dependent interpretation questions, not a mandatory clinical test menu.

anchors.text: Protein expression and HLA typing lie upstream of the displayed ligand. Antigen/HLA loss or impaired presentation can remove one recognition route; retaining another allele does not rescue a receptor requiring the lost allele. A different receptor using a retained allele needs its own specificity and functional evidence.

anchors.text: In a fictional target cell, HLA allele A is lost while B remains. An A-restricted receptor loses that route; a B-restricted receptor still needs its own peptide to be processed and displayed. B2M is the shared light chain for many class-I complexes, whereas class-II HLA uses different alpha and beta chains. Neither one lost allele nor a change in interferon-induced display establishes complete loss of baseline presentation. Test the required allele, antigen and display conditions with matched viable targets rather than infer recognition from the HLA label. A conventional surface-antigen CAR has another dependency, and reduced class I alone does not guarantee NK-cell killing.

anchors.text: Conventional surface-antigen CARs and peptide-HLA-directed receptors have different recognition requirements, but peptide-HLA CARs also exist. The WT1/HLA-A*24:02 CAR study is a preclinical counterexample to saying all intracellular source antigens are unreachable by any CAR. A format change does not supply a missing required peptide-HLA complex.

anchors.text:
CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

anchors.text: PD-1 on a T cell, when it meets PD-L1 on another cell, tells the T cell to stand down; CTLA-4 is often emphasised earlier, during priming, and PD-1 during ongoing responses in tissues, but these are overlapping emphases and not separate addresses. Reviews describe CTLA-4 as acting early in lymph nodes and PD-1 later in peripheral tissues, while CTLA-4 is also expressed on activated effector CD8 T cells (Buchbinder and Desai, 2016; Pardoll, 2012), and LAG-3, TIM-3 and TIGIT as co-inhibitory receptors with their own specialised functions (Anderson et al., 2016), so the early or late shorthand for CTLA-4 and PD-1 should not be stretched to them. Tumours coat themselves in PD-L1 and exploit this, and antibodies that block PD-1 (pembrolizumab, nivolumab), PD-L1 (atezolizumab, durvalumab) or CTLA-4 (ipilimumab) restore the attack, producing durable remissions in melanoma, lung, kidney, bladder and many other cancers since 2011. The price is autoimmune side effects when the brakes come off everywhere, and only a minority of patients respond, which drives the search for newer checkpoints (LAG-3, TIGIT) and combinations. The 'checkpoint' in 'cell-cycle checkpoint' is an unrelated concept. The checkpoints work through different contacts and are not interchangeable versions of PD-1. In reconstitution and cell experiments, PD-1 engaged by PD-L1 recruited the phosphatase Shp2, which dephosphorylated the co-receptor CD28 in preference to the T-cell receptor (Hui et al., 2017). PD-1 has two ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, and PD-L1 is found on leukocytes and on non-haematopoietic cells in non-lymphoid tissues as well as on cancer cells, and can be induced by interferon gamma (Buchbinder and Desai, 2016). In the current US prescribing information for pembrolizumab, the indication for high-risk early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (chemotherapy before surgery, then pembrolizumab alone afterwards) carries no PD-L1 qualifier, whereas the indications for locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic disease (with chemotherapy) and for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease (with sacituzumab govitecan) name a PD-L1 combined positive score of 10 or more as determined by an FDA-authorized test. That describes how the approved uses are worded and is not a trial finding about who benefits. CTLA-4 shares the ligands CD80 and CD86 with CD28 and can capture them from opposing cells by trans-endocytosis, so the neighbouring cell has fewer costimulatory ligands to offer (Qureshi et al., 2011). These descriptions concern the receptors' own contacts and are not a model of what a blocking antibody does or a prediction of clinical benefit. LAG-3 selectively recognised stable complexes of peptide and MHC class II and suppressed T cells responding to them, without recognising every class II complex or blocking CD4 binding (Maruhashi et al., 2018). Bat3 bound to and repressed TIM-3 function and protected helper T cells from galectin-9-mediated death, and in cell-line co-expression experiments galectin-9 abolished Bat3 binding to TIM-3 (Rangachari et al., 2012). TIGIT disrupted dimerisation of the costimulatory receptor CD226 on the same cell, and in mouse tumour and chronic-infection models combined TIGIT and PD-L1 antibody blockade enhanced CD8 T-cell function in a CD226-dependent way (Johnston et al., 2014). Staining for a checkpoint measures a component in sampled cells and not ligand contact or causal inhibition: PD-1-positive cells need not all be exhausted or cancer-reactive, more staining does not prove more inhibition or greater drug benefit, and TIM-3-positive cells do not select TIM-3 over PD-1 blockade. A checkpoint inhibitor interrupts one pathway: it does not teach T cells a new target, build a route into the tumour or repair every dysfunctional cell, and changing normal regulation can also harm healthy organs.

anchors.text: Checkpoint antibodies interrupt specified inhibitory contacts. PD-1 is a receptor with two partners, PD-L1 and PD-L2; PD-L1 is a distinct molecule found on cancer and non-cancer cells. The pembrolizumab label describes blockade of PD-1 binding to both ligands. Atezolizumab instead binds PD-L1 and blocks its PD-1 and B7.1 interactions; directly blocking PD-L1 does not directly block the separate PD-1/PD-L2 contact. These target-specific descriptions are more precise than treating all checkpoint drugs as one switch.

anchors.text: The pathways also differ inside and between cells. Hui's 2017 biochemical reconstitution and intact-cell experiments found that PD-1-recruited Shp2 preferentially dephosphorylated CD28 over the T-cell receptor, not that CD28 was the only possible affected signal. CTLA-4 and CD28 share CD80 and CD86. Qureshi's human and mouse cell experiments showed CTLA-4 capture and removal of these ligands from an opposing cell, reducing available costimulation. Contact and capture cartoons show these distinct receptor jobs; their molecule counts and positions are schematic, not a complete mechanism or a clinical comparison of blocking antibodies.

anchors.text: CTLA-4 is often emphasised during priming in lymphoid sites and PD-1 during ongoing responses in tissues. These are overlapping emphases, not exclusive addresses: CD28-related regulation can also matter later. LAG-3, TIM-3 and TIGIT have their own biology rather than being interchangeable versions of PD-1. A regulator identified in an experimental model does not establish benefit from blocking it in another population; each intervention needs its own evidence.

anchors.text: In a fictional sample containing PD-1-positive T cells, staining does not identify every cell's target, functional state or capacity to respond to an antibody. It does not show that all those cells are exhausted or that a drug will awaken all of them. Similarly, interrupting inhibition cannot alone solve a missing target-display component. Checkpoint biology, drug action, marker measurement and prediction of clinical benefit are separate claims.

anchors.text: Checkpoint blockade changes an inhibitory interaction; it does not install a new recognition receptor or reconstruct required HLA machinery that has been genetically lost. That last statement concerns missing machinery, not a claim that checkpoint treatment can never affect regulated HLA expression. Recognition, access and cell state remain separate dependencies. Vaccines, engineered cell receptors and cytokines change different inputs, and a plausible combination still needs regimen-specific benefit and safety evidence.

anchors.text: The multiple-controls analogy has two possible branches: interrupting regulation can support useful cancer-directed activity and can also injure healthy tissue. Neither outcome is guaranteed for a person. Normal checkpoint regulation helps limit immune injury, and immune-related adverse events can involve several organs. Assess activity, durability and harms in the relevant population rather than equating more immune activity with exclusively tumour-directed benefit.

anchors.text: The October 2026 U.S. label separates safety populations. Among 2,799 single-agent recipients in pooled melanoma and lung-cancer trials, hypothyroidism occurred in 8% (237/2,799) and adrenal insufficiency in 0.8% (22/2,799). Those are not TNBC-specific rates. In KEYNOTE-522, 778 people received pembrolizumab with the perioperative strategy, and adverse reactions led to its discontinuation in 20%. Immune-mediated reactions can begin after stopping treatment. For neoadjuvant TNBC use, the label calls for blood cortisol monitoring at baseline, before surgery and when clinically indicated; these labelled monitoring instructions are separate from a prediction of individual benefit or harm.

anchors.text: Use the cycle to name the measured step and the next untested dependency. A proposed bottleneck or complementary pair of mechanisms does not establish a beneficial or safe combination. Increasing a response can also affect healthy tissue; the model does not identify a safe intervention by itself.

anchors.text: Combining drugs is a hypothesis that must address the measured failure at useful exposures and tolerable harm. NCI notes both the rationale for combinations and the possibility of serious targeted-treatment side effects. Different pathway targets do not guarantee nonoverlapping toxicity or clinical rescue. A later variant found in a fictional progression sample is especially hard to interpret if the earlier sample lacked enough coverage to detect it: it may have been present but undetected, arisen later or be unrelated to the observed failure. First check the comparison and detection limit, then test its treatment-specific function. Detection, origin, timing and causation are separate conclusions.

anchors.text: In a fictional controlled comparison, both cultures have baseline class I; only the control increases its signal and surface display after interferon gamma. The candidate retains an interferon-alfa response, and restoring JAK2 restores the tested gamma response. With matched handling, viability and restoration controls, this supports a model-specific JAK2-dependent inducibility defect. It is not proof of a particular displayed peptide, safe clinical rescue, tumour access or useful killing. JAK1 and JAK2 have different interferon dependencies.

anchors.text: In Zaretsky’s selected four-person melanoma relapse series, two cases had JAK1 or JAK2 loss-of-function changes with loss of the normal allele and another had a truncating B2M change. The JAK2-deficient relapse cells failed to increase interferon-gamma signalling, PD-L1 and class I while retaining interferon-alfa/beta responsiveness. Engineered JAK1- or JAK2-deficient melanoma cells were still recognized by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Baseline display, inducibility, recognition and killing are separate dependencies; neither a JAK variant nor detectable HLA alone answers all of them.

anchors.text: An editing claim combines longitudinal populations or antigens, recognition or functional assays and relevant comparisons. Apparent antigen loss can instead reflect sampling, detection limits, expression change or another treatment. Neither sequencing alone nor a killing experiment reconstructs the whole history. One immune-rich sample, negative blood test or model cannot assign an individual postoperative phase, explain every recurrence or forecast personal risk; different lesions can face different pressures.

anchors.text: A useful investigation first checks exposure, assay performance and what the sample represents. It then compares earlier and later specimens, the sampled sites, coverage and detection limits, and candidate target, pathway, state or environmental changes. Controlled models can test target engagement, pathway activity, damage and survival separately. Genetic perturbation or rescue, an appropriate comparison compound, and removal/re-exposure can strengthen a causal explanation, but off-target effects and altered growth can confound it. Culture does not reproduce every tissue, immune, exposure or human-safety condition; clinical response assessment and mechanistic research remain distinct.

anchors.text: The adenosine route works outside cells. CD39 (ENTPD1) and CD73 (NT5E) are enzymes that help generate adenosine from extracellular ATP and ADP, and adenosine then acts on cell-surface receptors, including the A2A receptor on T cells. The enzymes can sit on immune cells, cancer cells or other tissue cells, so the source has to be measured and not assumed. The IDO route works inside a producing cell: IDO1 starts the breakdown of tryptophan along the kynurenine pathway. IDO is not an adenosine receptor and does not degrade ATP, so the two routes should not be merged into one 'suppressive axis'.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: In a fictional matched comparison, model A retains the source antigen, peptide-HLA display and tested receptor recognition, but the same cytotoxic drug causes less target death than before. Model B loses the required display while retaining its measured response to that drug. These locate different failed requirements: drug response in A and the tested immune-recognition route in B. They do not identify the complete cause, show that every immune route has failed or select a replacement treatment. Compare earlier and later material with compatible assays and matched exposure.

anchors.text: Immune surveillance concerns immune control of transformed cells. Immunoediting adds that immune pressure can alter which cancer populations persist. Elimination, equilibrium and escape describe processes that can coexist or occur independently, not a mandatory three-stage calendar. Shankaran’s genetically defined mouse experiments support lymphocyte and interferon-gamma contributions to control and selection. They do not measure what fraction of all human cancers immunity prevents.

anchors.text:
The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.

PD-L1 is not the only brake that follows the attack. Spranger and colleagues found in human melanoma that the T-cell-inflamed tumours were the ones with high indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), PD-L1 and regulatory T cells, and in mice that all three depended on CD8 T cells being present: IDO and PD-L1 through interferon gamma, and regulatory T cells through CCR4-binding chemokines with some induced proliferation. Their reading was that these pathways are driven by the immune response rather than orchestrated by the cancer cells.

Evidence from tissue. In human melanocytic lesions, 98% of PD-L1-positive (B7-H1-positive) tumours had tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes compared with 28% of PD-L1-negative tumours; positive melanocytes sat almost always immediately next to lymphocytes, and interferon gamma was detected at the interface but not in PD-L1-negative tumours (Taube and colleagues). The same colocalisation appeared in inflamed benign naevi, which fits PD-L1 as a response to tissue inflammation. In triple-negative breast cancer, Gruosso and colleagues described an immunoreactive group whose tumours had granzyme B-positive CD8 T cells inside cancer-cell regions, a type 1 interferon signature and elevated IDO and PD-L1, the pattern adaptive resistance predicts; that is an association in tissue and not a direct test of the loop. The alternative, called innate or constitutive resistance, is PD-L1 driven by the cancer cell's own signalling regardless of T cells.

A functionally important loss of JAK1 or JAK2 can impair the tumour cell response to interferon gamma. In four people with metastatic melanoma that relapsed on anti-PD-1 treatment, two relapse samples carried loss-of-function JAK1 or JAK2 mutations with deletion of the remaining normal allele, and truncating JAK1 or JAK2 mutations left the cells unresponsive to interferon gamma (Zaretsky and colleagues). The JAK2-deficient relapse cells lost interferon-gamma-induced PD-L1 and class-I increases but retained responses to interferon alfa and beta. In engineered melanoma cells, JAK1 or JAK2 loss did not abolish recognition by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Loss of inducibility is therefore different from absence of all baseline recognition. This selected series does not estimate a frequency for all cancers.

anchors.text: A PD-L1 stain measures protein on defined tumour and immune cells, not why it is present. Colocalization with lymphocytes and interferon-related expression can support induced expression, while a uniform lymphocyte-poor pattern raises other hypotheses; neither pattern proves a cause. Adding interferon gamma and measuring PD-L1 tests inducibility in a laboratory model. Appropriate pathway perturbations and controls investigate causation, and neither that assay nor a tissue score measures the entire in-vivo feedback loop or treatment benefit.

anchors.text: KEYNOTE-522 randomised 1,174 people with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer to pembrolizumab or placebo with chemotherapy before surgery, followed by continuation of the assigned antibody or placebo after surgery. At a median follow-up of 75.1 months, estimated 60-month overall survival was 86.6 per cent versus 81.7 per cent. Enrolment did not require PD-L1 positivity. The trial compared the whole perioperative regimen and was not designed to isolate the contribution of each treatment phase. These group results do not predict one person's outcome.

anchors.text: In KEYNOTE-522, patients with previously untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer received pembrolizumab or placebo with chemotherapy before surgery, followed by pembrolizumab or placebo after surgery. The pembrolizumab regimen improved event-free survival (Schmid et al., 2022) and overall survival (Schmid et al., 2024). These are results for the tested early-stage regimen, not evidence that a checkpoint marker alone establishes benefit in another setting.

anchors.text: KEYNOTE-355 studied 847 people with previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. In the PD-L1 combined-positive-score-at-least-10 subgroup, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 23.0 months versus 16.1 with placebo plus chemotherapy, with a death hazard ratio of 0.73. A median divides a study group in half; it is not an individual forecast. The October 2026 U.S. pembrolizumab label has no PD-L1 qualifier for its high-risk early-stage TNBC regimen, while its advanced TNBC indications with chemotherapy or sacituzumab govitecan specify CPS at least 10 and an FDA-authorised test. The sacituzumab combination is a separate labelled regimen, not the KEYNOTE-355 comparison. Population, regimen, scoring context and evidence must stay together.

anchors.text: The CPS-at-least-one analysis includes people with CPS at least ten. Its nonsignificant overall-survival comparison is therefore not an isolated result for CPS one to nine. Nested subgroup findings, the prespecified testing hierarchy and individual benefit are different questions; none establishes that every person below a cutoff has exactly zero treatment effect.

anchors.text: A chemokine can matter after entry. Chow found that CXCR3 and dendritic-cell-derived CXCL9 were required for productive anti-PD-1 responses in tumour-bearing mice but were not required for initial CD8 infiltration. This is different from Mikucki’s transferred-cell vascular-trafficking experiment. Name the tested step, model, stimulus and endpoint before treating the two studies as the same claim.

anchors.text: In mouse experiments, PD-L1 blockade re-engaged effector transcription with little remodelling of the exhausted chromatin landscape. Reinvigorated cells could become exhausted again under continued high antigen and did not simply become ordinary durable memory. Laboratory reinvigoration is distinct from universal reversal or patient benefit.

anchors.text: Design (NEJM 2020): 1,174 patients with untreated stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer randomised 2 to 1 to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo every 3 weeks with four cycles of paclitaxel and carboplatin then four of doxorubicin or epirubicin with cyclophosphamide, surgery, then nine cycles of adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo. Pathological complete response 64.8 versus 51.2 percent (first 602 patients); event-free survival at 36 months 84.5 versus 76.8 percent (hazard ratio 0.63, NEJM 2022); overall survival at 60 months 86.6 versus 81.7 percent (p 0.002, median follow-up 75.1 months, NEJM 2024). The preplanned exploratory residual-cancer-burden analysis (Annals of Oncology 2024) reported EFS hazard ratios for RCB-0, 1, 2 and 3 of 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.38 to 1.31), 0.92 (0.39 to 2.20), 0.52 (0.32 to 0.82) and 1.24 (0.69 to 2.23). These post-treatment strata can themselves be affected by treatment; their estimates do not separately randomise postoperative treatment or prove a benefit in every stratum.

anchors.text: The study question concerns the whole assigned sequence in previously untreated, non-metastatic stage II or III triple-negative breast cancer: T1c with N1 or N2, or T2 to T4 with N0 to N2, and performance status 0 or 1. The registry excludes prior checkpoint therapy and active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the preceding two years, among other criteria. There was one assignment of 784 people to pembrolizumab and 390 to placebo across preoperative chemotherapy, surgery and postoperative treatment, without a separate postoperative randomisation. Smaller node-negative tumours outside those entry criteria and metastatic disease are different settings. Entry did not require PD-L1 selection, and the high-risk early-stage indication in the prescribing information has no PD-L1 threshold.

anchors.text: At the fourth planned interim analysis reported in 2022, median follow-up was 39.1 months and all 1,174 participants contributed to the assigned-group survival comparison. Estimated 36-month EFS was 84.5% (95% confidence interval 81.7 to 86.9) versus 76.8% (72.2 to 80.7), with hazard ratio 0.63 (0.48 to 0.82). From the rounded survival estimates, the three-year absolute gain is 7.7 points, approximately eight additional people alive and event-free per 100, and number needed to treat is 1/0.077, about 13. The corresponding event risks are 15.5% versus 23.2%, a relative risk reduction of about 33%; the model's 37% lower hazard is a different measure.

anchors.text: The final overall-survival analysis published in 2024 used a March 22, 2024 cutoff and median follow-up of 75.1 months. Estimated 60-month OS was 86.6% versus 81.7%, with the paper reporting P=0.002; the label reports an OS hazard ratio of 0.66 (95% confidence interval 0.50 to 0.87) for the prespecified analysis. The absolute difference is 4.9 points, about five additional people alive per 100 at five years. Its reciprocal is 20.4, or 21 when rounding up to a whole-person number needed to treat. Neither this result nor the three-year EFS calculation identifies who benefits or combines benefit with harms. Comparing the 13.6-point pCR, 7.7-point EFS and 4.9-point OS gains does not show an effect shrinking over time: their endpoints, cohorts and horizons differ.

anchors.text: Design (Lancet 2020): 847 patients randomised 2 to 1 to pembrolizumab or placebo with nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine and carboplatin at 209 sites in 29 countries; the registry participant-flow table lists 35 starters across the three part-1 groups (11, 14 and 10) and 847 in the randomised part-2 groups (566 and 281), matching 882 total enrolments. Progression-free survival in CPS 10 or more 9.7 versus 5.6 months (hazard ratio 0.65); final overall survival (NEJM 2022) 23.0 versus 16.1 months in CPS 10 or more (hazard ratio 0.73, p 0.0185), 17.6 versus 16.0 in CPS 1 or more (0.86, not significant) and 17.2 versus 15.5 overall (0.89, not tested). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events 68.1 versus 66.9 percent.

anchors.text: Keep the analysis cohorts separate. The 2020 first-interim pCR comparison used the first 602 randomised participants: 64.8% versus 51.2%, estimated difference 13.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval 5.4 to 21.8). The sponsor-posted first-1,002 comparison is 64.0% versus 54.7%, with a stratified difference of 9.2 points (2.8 to 15.6). That reported adjusted estimate is not simple subtraction of the rounded percentages. The current label also presents an all-1,174 pCR comparison, 63.0% versus 55.6%, estimated difference 7.5 points (1.6 to 13.4). These are different specified analysis populations, not interchangeable response claims.

anchors.text: The combined positive score is the number of PD-L1-staining tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages divided by the total number of viable tumour cells, multiplied by 100 (Cortes 2022). KEYNOTE-355 randomised 847 patients with untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer 2:1 to pembrolizumab or placebo with the investigator's chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel or gemcitabine-carboplatin), with PD-L1 tested centrally by the 22C3 assay. Progression-free survival at the interim analysis was 9.7 against 5.6 months in the CPS 10 or more group (hazard ratio 0.65, primary objective met), 7.6 against 5.6 months in CPS 1 or more (0.74, not significant) and 7.5 against 5.6 months overall (0.82, not tested), the effect increasing with PD-L1 enrichment (Cortes 2020). At the final analysis (median follow-up 44.1 months) overall survival in the CPS 10 group was 23.0 against 16.1 months (hazard ratio 0.73, significant), 17.6 against 16.0 months in CPS 1 or more (0.86, not significant) and 17.2 against 15.5 months in all patients (0.89, not tested); grade 3 to 5 treatment-related events occurred in 68.1 against 66.9 percent (Cortes 2022). NICE recommends pembrolizumab with paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel for untreated triple-negative locally recurrent unresectable or metastatic breast cancer in the population the appraisal covers (TA801, June 2022). A different assay and score defined the earlier atezolizumab result: IMpassion130 used the SP142 immune-cell score with positivity at 1 percent or more of the tumour area; median progression-free survival was 7.5 against 5.0 months and overall survival 25.0 against 15.5 months in the PD-L1-positive subgroup, without a significant overall survival gain in the whole population (Schmid 2018), and the parent page's history records that approval was later withdrawn. Early disease needs no PD-L1 test: in KEYNOTE-522 pembrolizumab with chemotherapy raised pathological complete response from 51.2 to 64.8 percent in stage II and III disease unselected for PD-L1 (Schmid 2020) and five-year overall survival from 81.7 to 86.6 percent (Schmid 2024); NICE TA851 (December 2022) recommends it for triple-negative early or locally advanced breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. The biomarker readout pd-l1-cps carries the label wording for every CPS threshold across cancers.

anchors.text: Label safety (Keytruda, 778 treated patients): serious adverse reactions 44 percent, fatal 0.9 percent, discontinuation of pembrolizumab 20 percent, most often for raised transaminases and rash.

anchors.text: Safety also retains its report and denominator. Across treatment phases, the 2020 paper reported treatment-related grade 3 or higher events in 78.0% versus 73.0%, including treatment-related deaths in 0.4% versus 0.3%. The label describes 778 versus 389 participants receiving at least one dose, distinct from the 784 versus 390 assigned. Its adverse-reaction categories and fatal-event figures must not be substituted for the paper's treatment-related categories. The prescribing information warns that immune-mediated reactions can arise after treatment stops and that hypothyroidism may require long-term hormone replacement. Event frequency, severity, duration, discontinuation and quality of life remain separate parts of the comparison.

anchors.text: The co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response at surgery, defined as ypT0/Tis ypN0, and event-free survival from randomisation. The response definition permits residual in-situ disease in the breast while excluding invasive residual cancer in breast and nodes. Event-free survival counts progression preventing definitive surgery, local or distant recurrence, a second primary cancer or death from any cause; overall survival is a secondary endpoint counting death from any cause. Because death is part of EFS, it is an event rather than a competing event for that composite. Analysing a recurrence component alone can require a different competing-risk question.

anchors.text: The earlier adaptive phase 2 I-SPY2 report estimated pCR of 60% versus 22% in its triple-negative subgroup against its own chemotherapy control. That is a different comparison from KEYNOTE-522 and cannot establish a cross-trial treatment ranking. Likewise, better survival among people who achieve pCR is a prognostic association within selected response groups, not proof of the postoperative drug's separate effect or a validated rule selecting individual benefit. CTNeoBC found a strong pCR-outcome association but did not validate pCR as a trial-level surrogate for EFS or OS in its included trials. Here survival itself was measured.

anchors.text: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

anchors.text: Keep the identities and preparation of both effector and target cells, whether a cell line, engineered target or patient-derived preparation, together with medium, effector-to-target ratio and exposure time. Culture can change the tested population. The output might be a fraction of identified targets dead, a viable target count, release under a specified normalisation, or a time curve; these are different quantities. A negative is interpretable only when cell health, target suitability and controls support the experiment, and no universal laboratory killing cut-off establishes clinical efficacy. Reproducibility and biological specificity need checking for the specimen, model and intended claim.

anchors.text: Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

anchors.text: Reading guide (definitions plus OnCo inference). Detection asks whether a cell was found, segmentation asks which pixels belong to it, and phenotyping classifies the cell afterwards; finding a nucleus does not give a reliable whole-cell boundary. Intersection over union is the area two masks share divided by the area either covers, from 0 to 1, and a single value can hide missed or merged cells, so check object counts and characteristic errors too. A mask assigns existing signals to estimated regions and is not a measurement of a new marker. Merging, splitting and missing cells distort counts, marker combinations and spatial relations, so overlay masks on the original channels.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: Fixed sections and morphology or selected stains can measure identity, compartment and abundance; viable-cell assays ask about phenotype and function. Dissociation loses native location, culture can select populations and tests consume finite material. Keep cells per square millimetre, specified cell fractions, stromal-area percentages and assay-specific function distinct. TIL therapy is a manufactured expanded-cell product: a tissue count does not establish product yield, composition, potency or treatment success. Sampling, damage, mixed compartments, unsuitable markers and culture selection are different failure modes, and descriptive pathology, research function and clinical treatment selection require different validation.

anchors.text: The National Library of Medicine distinguishes mononuclear leukocytes from granulocytes and from monocytes alone. A primary study of immune monitoring in HIV vaccine research found that processing and cryopreservation conditions affected cell recovery, viability and measured antigen responses. Those were assay findings, not a validated cancer-treatment predictor. A blood preparation also samples a different compartment from a tumor biopsy; the specimen and handling conditions belong with its interpretation.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: A stored PBMC sample is a finite specimen. It does not establish immune infiltration of a tumour, preserve every function or population equally, identify antigen specificity, or guarantee enough material for every later test. In the fictional equal-viability comparison, losing monocytes can affect a whole-protein stimulation because antigen-presenting-cell composition matters; viability alone does not establish interchangeable inputs. Fit and acceptance rules belong to the intended downstream assay.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: Historical method examples establish what was measured in those experiments. Giesen and colleagues reported simultaneous imaging of 32 proteins and protein modifications at subcellular resolution in human breast-cancer samples in 2014, using metal-tagged antibodies and high-resolution laser ablation coupled to mass cytometry. Ablation consumes the sampled area. The 32-marker example is not a present instrument ceiling, and Lin and colleagues' 2018 t-CyCIF study used conventional optical microscopes for up to 60-plex images of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded specimens. Each example retains its method, molecular layer and preparation.

anchors.text: Fictional worked example (two stipulated cells). One mask covers a small T cell and an adjacent cancer cell, so one table row reports both an immune marker and keratin; that is a merged object, not a hybrid cell. A split into three objects for two cells adds objects, not cells. Correcting the mask may show two neighbouring cells, and their proximity still does not prove immune recognition.

anchors.text: Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. Read counts are not always cell counts, because preparation, amplification and transcript abundance can change them, and absolute expansion needs compatible cell-number evidence. A sequence overlap between blood and tumour is detected overlap under a clonotype definition and is not a target, and antigen specificity needs a matching controlled recognition experiment.

anchors.text: A repertoire report can give a clonotype list, relative frequencies, diversity, clonality and overlap, but there is no universal expansion or clonality threshold that proves tumour specificity. A sequence found in dissociated tumour material does not locate its cell inside a cancer-cell nest. Not detected means absent from the assay result under its sampling and calling rules, while an observed overlap or change nominates a receptor for a separate controlled recognition experiment.

anchors.text: Repertoire sequencing can describe richness and the distribution of sampled receptor sequences. Those summaries depend on the sampled population and the way receptor identities and counts are defined; the original sequencing study found diversity estimates that differed from earlier methods. A repertoire dominated by a clone is a distributional observation. It is distinct from proving tumor specificity, a malignant clone or successful tumor killing, each of which needs additional evidence.

anchors.text: Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

anchors.text: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text: Cytokine-positive percentages need a named parent gate, and fluorescence intensity uses instrument-dependent units. Poor recovery, handling delays, signal overlap, altered staining after fixation or permeabilisation, background and scarce events can make a small positive population unstable, and inhibitor timing belongs to the protocol. Minimum event counts, positivity boundaries and clinical interpretation need validation for the panel, stimulus and population; there is no universal double-positive percentage that proves tumour killing or treatment benefit.

anchors.text: In an invented vaccine report, one blood clonotype becomes more frequent, its sequence also appears in sampled tumour, a separately tested cell mixture responds to added peptide, and ctDNA becomes undetectable. These are four observations, not proof that this clone killed the cancer. Link the responding cells to a compatible paired receptor, test natural tumour recognition and target death, and preserve each assay's denominator and detection limit. Surgery, chemotherapy, shedding and sampling can also affect ctDNA. Conversely, an unchanged blood repertoire does not exclude a response in unsampled tissue. Temporal coincidence does not establish the causal contribution of one clone.

anchors.text: In a fictional report, A rises from 0.1% to 2.0% of sampled blood receptors and is 0.5% in sampled tumour; its blood share rose twentyfold. B changes from 3.0% to 3.1% and is not detected in that tumour sample. A is a candidate, while neither the large B share nor overlap for A identifies an antigen. If a separate mixed-cell peptide assay is positive, it has not assigned that response to A. Link the same cells and compatible paired alpha-beta receptor to a controlled peptide-HLA response, then test naturally presenting targets, killing and cross-reactivity. Relative frequency is not absolute cell expansion, and non-detection in one sample is not whole-body absence.

anchors.text: Immunodominance is a contextual hierarchy of measured responses, distinct from encoded target count and from epitope spreading. Presentation, precursor frequency, repertoire, priming, HLA, delivery, immune history, tissue and time can change the hierarchy. A favourable binding prediction does not establish immunogenicity, and more encoded targets do not guarantee balanced immunity or independent tumour coverage.

anchors.text: A measured hierarchy needs offered targets, compartment, cell denominator, baseline, timing, matched per-target stimulation, background and positive controls. Detection thresholds and in vitro expansion can alter apparent ranking. Peptide response is not evidence of natural tumour display or tumour-cell killing.

anchors.text: Epitope spreading is additional detected recognition beyond the initially targeted epitope set, potentially within one source protein or across proteins. More response to the same target is expansion. Responses to both directly encoded A and B do not themselves demonstrate spreading. Newly detected is not newly created: baseline sensitivity can miss pre-existing responsive cells.

anchors.text: Tumour injury can release additional antigen for uptake and presentation, but one follow-up response does not establish that entire causal chain. Define peptide-HLA targets and compare matched baseline and follow-up assays with background, presentation and cross-reactivity controls; assess intervening treatment. Vaccine recruitment or expansion does not normally rewrite mature TCRs. An immune response, including one to healthy self, does not establish recurrence prevention, safety or clinical benefit.

anchors.text: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is made up of DNA fragments shed by tumour cells into the bloodstream, where they form only a small fraction of all cell-free DNA and are detected with sensitive sequencing. Its uses span genotyping for companion diagnostics, tracking resistance mutations such as EGFR T790M and ESR1, molecular residual disease, early detection and response monitoring. Shedding varies with tumour type and burden, and clonal haematopoiesis can confound results. The term underpins the Liquid biopsy (ctDNA), MRD / molecular residual disease testing and Multi-cancer early detection (MCED) technologies, and it appears in the SERENA-6, CIRCULATE-Japan and IMvigor011 trials and in ideas on molecular-progression switching beyond ESR1 and HPV ctDNA to guide cervical cancer therapy.
anchors.sourceScope: Specified current reads where named; inherited fields retain prior recorded source scope. Containment does not independently verify every older assertion in a field.

anchors.text:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

anchors.text: Assay card: measures receptor identities, usually by the complementarity-determining region 3 of the variable region, and their measured representation in the sampled population. How: extract nucleic acid, amplify or capture receptor regions, sequence, then group and count under stated rules, which may use nucleotide or amino-acid sequence, gene segments, one chain or paired chains. Input: blood cells or tissue nucleic acid for bulk methods and compatible cell preparations for single-cell methods, and preparation consumes material. A high-resolution human repertoire method reported chain diversity without sequence-associated or quantitative restrictions (Ruggiero 2015). Failure modes: poor material, shallow sampling, amplification bias, chain mismatch, inconsistent definitions and batch effects. It cannot tell every receptor's target, tissue position, killing or benefit, and a research method is not automatically a treatment-selection test.

anchors.text: Handling is evidence: in HIV vaccine assay studies, the time from venipuncture to cryopreservation was the most important parameter, and blood processed at 24 hours compared with within 8 hours lost on average about 8% of PBMC viability, about 32% of cell recovery and 36% to 56% of interferon gamma T-cell frequencies by ELISpot, which led the authors to recommend cryopreservation within 8 hours (Bull 2007). That is a finding for those protocols and assays and is not a universal schedule for cancer assays. A rapidly processed baseline and a delayed follow-up can therefore confound a biological comparison, and a high viability percentage alone does not show that every population or function was preserved.

anchors.text: Spot size or intensity is not a measure of target-cell killing. A negative result remains bounded by the number and condition of input cells, the stimulus, chosen secreted molecule, culture history and response rule; it is not a census of every responding cell in the body. Assay reproducibility and a cancer-treatment benefit claim need separate evidence.

anchors.text: The repertoire is a distribution of receptor identities and abundances in a stated population and time. A clone is a cellular lineage; a clonotype is an operational sequence grouping. Single-chain labels and paired identities have different resolution. V(D)J assembly and thymic selection contribute diversity, while expansion changes abundance; diversity and total T-cell count are different quantities.

anchors.text: T cells are a lymphocyte family, not every white cell or every lymphocyte. Precursors develop through the thymus, with receptor generation and selection shaping the peripheral pool. Conventional alpha-beta cells recognise peptide-HLA; gamma-delta cells use another, context-dependent receptor system, so conventional peptide-HLA examples do not describe every T cell.

anchors.text: For a coding change to supply a conventional T-cell target, its information must be expressed, protein produced and processed into a fragment, that peptide displayed with HLA, and a suitable receptor able to recognise the display. DNA, RNA, protein, recovered displayed peptide and controlled recognition are separate observations. A prediction at one step does not measure all the others. This conventional alpha-beta route does not describe every T cell, antibody or natural killer recognition system.

anchors.text: Blood, tumour and lymph nodes sample overlapping but different populations. Infection, therapy, age and movement can change a sample; absence from one tube may reflect sampling or detection rather than whole-body absence. A pretreatment blood sample is not a complete stored repertoire. Lower measured diversity after infection may reflect a vigorous response and does not establish cancer specificity, vaccine causation or uniformly worse immunity.

anchors.text: Nucleotide and amino-acid clonotypes need not be the same grouping. The standard genetic code assigns several codons to the same amino acid, so different nucleotide sequences can encode the same receptor segment; amino-acid identity alone is not proof of one cellular lineage. MIGEC introduced molecular-identifier groups to correct PCR and sequencing errors in antibody and T-cell receptor repertoire profiling (Shugay 2014). Such error correction does not restore molecules absent from the sample. Report which chain, grouping rule and abundance unit the method actually used.

anchors.text: TIL is a location label, CD8 is a phenotype and antigen specificity is another property. Simoni found bystander CD8 cells recognizing viral rather than cancer epitopes in human lung and colorectal tumours; the study’s CD39 associations are not a universal test of every cell’s target. A functional assay compares defined effectors and targets with recognition and target-survival controls. Neither presence, cytokine release nor one killing assay reproduces every access barrier or establishes clinical benefit.

anchors.text: Receptor sequencing asks which receptor sequences are represented and in what relative abundance. ELISpot asks how many input cells release the chosen molecule under the stated stimulation. An expanded sequence does not establish that it caused a spot, and a spot in mixed cells does not identify a receptor sequence. Connecting identity to recognition or killing requires additional experiments with suitable controls.

anchors.text: Fictional matched receptor samples contain 10 clonotype A cells among 1,000 T cells (1%) and 10 among 100 (10%). The sampled count remains 10; the changed denominator drives the larger fraction. Absolute expansion requires comparable sampling and calibrated counts, and neither frequency identifies antigen. State sampling depth, chain definition, compartment, method and timing.

anchors.text: Selecting and expanding native antigen-reactive cells retains their existing receptors; introducing selected receptor coding sequences is receptor engineering. The two approaches can share discovery assays while differing in manufacturing and product-specific safety and release requirements. A banked research aliquot or a favourable receptor result alone does not establish that a viable, suitable and releasable therapeutic product can later be manufactured.

anchors.text: Yee, Lizee and Schueneman describe three ways of adoptive T-cell transfer: tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes taken from a biopsy; lymphocytes redirected by a chimeric antigen receptor or T-cell receptor; and the isolation and expansion of often low-frequency endogenous T cells reactive to tumour antigens from the peripheral blood, which they call endogenous T-cell (ETC) therapy (Cancer Journal 2015). It needs specialised methods to isolate and expand very low-frequency tumour-reactive T cells from blood, and the authors note that a trial can be started quickly once a tumour-associated target epitope has been identified (Cancer Journal 2015). The early melanoma trials at Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center infused such cells as clones against MART-1, gp100, tyrosinase and NY-ESO-1.

anchors.text: Measurement card: input is a sequencing-derived clonotype table and the calculation consumes no further tissue, though the upstream assay consumes its sample. Output units are a count for richness, dimensionless values for entropy and normalised clonality, and an effective clonotype count for effective diversity. Controls are matched compartments and handling, chain definition, error filtering, abundance units (reads, corrected molecules or cells are not automatically equivalent), depth assessment and replicates or resampling. Subsampling to a comparable depth helps assess sampling effects but cannot recover cells never sampled. A clonality summary does not identify what the receptors recognise, whether cells killed tumour, or whether treatment helped, and there is no universal clonality score that means an immune therapy is working.

anchors.text: Pogorelyy and colleagues used longitudinal sampling in three pairs of identical twins after yellow-fever vaccination and identified 600 to 1,700 responding clonotypes per donor. The three validation approaches were applied to donor S1: enrichment in an activated-cell subset, interferon-gamma secretion and a specified peptide-HLA dextramer. Together they validated 395 of 773 expanded clonotypes by at least one approach. This does not mean all candidates in every donor were functionally confirmed or that one fold-change rule validates cancer specificity.

anchors.text: Robins and colleagues sequenced millions of rearranged beta-chain genes from two adults and estimated at least four times the diversity found by previous approaches. That method comparison is not a complete inventory of any person's receptors. VDJdb aggregates published specificity assays; an annotation match should retain the actual sequence/chain, paired-receptor information where available, HLA and experimental context. A match is a lead for verification, and lack of an annotation is not proof of no relevant specificity.

anchors.text: In research, test paired receptor expression and naturally presenting targets, with relevant antigen/HLA removal and restoration, irrelevant peptides, unmodified effectors and healthy tissue. Multimer or peptide-loaded reagent binding is different from natural processing, target-cell death or patient benefit. This research validation is distinct from the approved product’s clinical testing rule.

anchors.text:
Chen and Mellman’s 2013 framework describes seven linked steps: release of cancer antigens; their collection and presentation; T-cell priming and activation; trafficking; entry into tumour tissue; recognition of cancer cells; and killing. Further antigen release may support another round. In conventional T-cell recognition, a displayed peptide-HLA complex and a suitable T-cell receptor are separate dependencies.

This is a T-cell-centred organizing model, not a universal route, assay result or treatment-selection algorithm. Steps overlap, priming may occur away from the tumour, and other immune mechanisms require their own account. Checkpoints and local tissue conditions affect several steps. Vaccines aim to generate or expand reactive responses, checkpoint drugs interrupt selected inhibitory signals, and engineered cells provide a recognition system and effectors. Each still needs appropriate targets, access, function and safety evidence.

anchors.text: In a fictional biopsy, PD-L1 is found at a lymphocyte-rich border but not at the centre. That distribution is consistent with induced expression; it does not prove the proposed loop. A negative region does not establish absence of immune attack elsewhere, and other inhibitory pathways may operate. A positive PD-L1 result alone also cannot distinguish induced from constitutive expression.

anchors.text: The postoperative-only question remains distinct: OptimICE-pCR randomises people after pCR to postoperative pembrolizumab or observation, and the registry lists it as recruiting with no posted results. KEYNOTE-522 did not randomise dropping a chemotherapy component. CREATE-X compared postoperative capecitabine with standard postsurgical treatment after residual HER2-negative disease, while OlympiA compared olaparib with placebo in eligible high-risk germline BRCA1/2-associated HER2-negative disease after chemotherapy and local treatment. Those reports describe their own comparisons rather than a randomised test of adding either drug to the KEYNOTE-522 sequence. No result here is a personal forecast or a treatment-omission rule.

anchors.text: The mitochondrial route uses BCL-2-family control of BAX and BAK and cytochrome c release. In cell experiments, combined BAX and BAK loss blocked mitochondrial responses to several apoptotic stimuli; this does not establish resistance to all forms of death. Death-receptor signals provide another route. Apoptosis is not inherently immune-silent: anthracycline-treated tumour cells showed calreticulin-dependent immunogenicity in mouse experiments. A death marker, a mitochondrial response and sustained killing answer different questions. Protein abundance alone cannot establish dependence or choose a treatment.

anchors.text: Necrotic appearance can follow overwhelming injury or regulated death mechanisms. A late membrane-integrity measurement cannot reconstruct the preceding death sequence. Histology describes the sampled region; necrosis there does not establish the absence of viable tumour elsewhere, treatment success or a particular molecular pathway. Distinguish tissue appearance from a mechanism established by controlled perturbation and complementary readouts. Inflammation and antigen-specific adaptive immune protection are separate outcomes.
